subject: BrightCart launch: traffic scaling pledge & temporary quota ops
messages:
From: Joshua Park <joshua@brightcart.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: BrightCart launch traffic: provisional uplift request

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from the launch engineering team — we just finalized the feature flip schedule for BrightCart's new checkout AI (go-live: 2028-09-20). Estimated ingestion: 2.1M inference calls/day during week 1, spiking to ~4.8M on peak promo hours. Attached is our high-level projection and hourly SLOs.

Can Redwood provision a temporary quota uplift for the first two weeks (we're asking for 3x our baseline) and a short canary window with prioritized throughput? We want to avoid backpressure during the promo.

Also: any guidance on recommended model variants (quantized vs full) to balance latency/cost for our use case would help.

Thanks,
Joshua Park
Product Lead — Checkout AI
BrightCart

Date: 2028-08-14T17:12:00Z

Team — forwarding BrightCart's ask. Key asks: temporary 3x uplift for 09/20 go-live, prioritized canary throughput, model guidance.

Proposed ops play:
- Temporary quota window 2028-09-20 -> 2028-10-04 (2 weeks).
- Canary days 1–2 with 50% traffic throttled to warm caches (we'll coordinate with SRE).
- Fallback policy: route to quantized v2 if we hit latencies > 300ms p95.

Ben: can you validate capacity and confirm whether we can reserve a dedicated burst pool and what the billing/showback looks like?
Karthik: can you lead customer comms and confirm acceptance criteria for the canary?
Grace: product question — what do we need to enable on the model side to support an automatic fallback to quantized variant?

I attached their projection; Joshua, I'll loop product & ops and get back with a concrete entitlement ask by EOD tomorrow.

— Marissa
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-15T09:38:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightCart launch traffic: provisional uplift request

Marissa — ran numbers with infra. Short answer: we can commit a burst pool sized to handle the 4.8M peak if we reserve 48 GPU-hours/day across the two-week window. Notes:

- Capacity: allocate 8x A100-equivalent slots in the burst pool, pre-warmed for the 72-hour canary.
- Cost impact: estimated additional usage bill approx $42k for the two-week uplift (will show on usage). We can do a one-time uplift credit if Sales wants to negotiate.
- Ops: SRE needs a concrete warmup plan (cache priming + synthetic ramp) and a circuit-breaker to failover to quantized endpoints after 3 consecutive p95 latency > 350ms.

I'll mark this as provisionally available pending product confirmation on fallback behavior.

Ben
Director, Capacity & Operations
Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-16T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightCart launch traffic: provisional uplift request

Thanks — a few product/engineering clarifications from my side:

1) Fallback routing: we can support automatic routing based on observed latency via the runtime feature flag. We'll need a model pair registered:
   - primary: checkout-v3 (full precision)
   - fallback: checkout-v3-q4 (4-bit quantized)
   The runtime can switch traffic at the request-router layer with no client change, but we need model pinning and a migrations manifest.

2) Prefetching & KV caching: to minimize cold-start p99, BrightCart should provide representative prompts for prefix caching. We can pre-populate KV caches during the 72h warmup.

3) Quality guardrail: quantify expected degradation for quantized variant. Ops wants a degradation threshold (e.g., recall drop <= 2.5%) to trigger automatic fallback — Sales should lock this with the customer.

Action items:
- Karthik: capture the recall/latency SLAs BrightCart accepts for the fallback policy.
- Marissa: confirm whether BrightCart signed the MPA (I saw a scanned copy in the drive; if signed we'll need legal copied).

Grace
Senior PM, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Joshua Park <joshua@brightcart.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-12T16:45:00Z
Subject: BrightCart launch: cadence confirmation + entitlement ask (final)

Joshua — thanks for the projection. We're aligned on the operational plan and have a final entitlement ask for BrightCart to approve. Summary: 

1) Temporary Quota/Uplift: 3x baseline throughput for 2028-09-20 -> 2028-10-04. This maps to a reserved burst pool (8 A100-equivalent slots) with pre-warm for 72 hours pre-go-live.
2) Canary & Rollout: Day 1–2 canary at 50% traffic, synthetic ramp by BrightCart SRE to exercise caches. Full ramp Day 3 if canary metrics are green.
3) Fallback Policy: auto-route to checkout-v3-q4 after 3 consecutive p95 latency breaches > 350ms OR observed model degradation > 2.5% recall.
4) Billing & Credits: estimated uplift usage charge ~$42k; Redwood can offer a one-time usage credit of $15k if BrightCart commits to a 3-month Reserved Minimum.

Please confirm the MPA signature and acceptance of the canary criteria by EOD 2028-09-14 so Ops can create the entitlement and schedule the warmup. Attaching the signed MPA stub here for legal intake.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
